name: Waterfall.io
verdict: Keys appear to be issued by Waterfall's team after a call, so email them for access and pricing. Customers do not connect accounts; you use your own key, with usage-based pricing.
needGuide: Yes — contact Waterfall for access and pricing first; no self-serve key was found.

auth.detail: API key in the x-api-key header against https://api.waterfall.io (the marketing page shows two header spellings, the docs say x-api-key). A master key can create and manage sub-keys for teams or workflows. Async endpoints return a job_id; results come via a Finder call or a signed webhook (Ed25519, verified with a public JWKS endpoint). No OAuth.

effort.timeToFirstTest: unknown (depends on Waterfall issuing a key)
effort.timeToProduction: unknown, likely days after the onboarding call

approval.gate: Keys appear to be issued by Waterfall's team after a call (the docs say to contact them for access and pricing). Pricing is usage-based with no monthly commitment or credit expiry, but figures are not published. Customers do not connect accounts.

scopes.why: No scopes documented; sub-keys partition access and usage.
scopes.summary: No scopes documented; sub-keys partition access and usage.

cost: Usage-based pricing quoted by sales; no published prices
prerequisites: Account and owner: Whoever holds the master key owns the account and can create sub-keys. Use a company-owned contact and shared mailbox.
Where you register: Contact support@waterfall.io or book a call on waterfall.io to receive the first (master) API key; no self-serve signup was documented
Cost: Usage-based pricing quoted by sales; no published prices

registerAt.path: Contact support@waterfall.io or book a call on waterfall.io to receive the first (master) API key; no self-serve signup was documented

steps.do: Email support@waterfall.io or book a call to request API access and pricing
Store the master key in a secrets manager and create sub-keys per environment via the API Key Management endpoints
Call POST /v1/prospector or contact enrichment with x-api-key and a webhook_url
Implement webhook verification with the Ed25519 JWKS and polling fallback via job_id
Review data-privacy obligations for enriched contact data (emails, phones)

roles.team: Whoever holds the master key owns the account and can create sub-keys. Use a company-owned contact and shared mailbox.
roles.console: Sub-keys via API Key Management endpoints (list, create, update) using the master key.
roles.customer: None for the standard model. Sub-keys could separate your customers' usage, but this was not documented.

testing: No sandbox or test mode is documented.
Ask support about trial credits and use small batches.
Test webhook delivery with signature verification against the public JWKS.

blockers.fix: The first key requires contacting Waterfall; start early.

blockers.problem: Rate limits and sandbox are not documented

blockers.fix: Confirm a lawful basis and opt-out handling.
Handle webhook failures by polling job_id results.

automation.agentCan: Draft the access request email, write the client, webhook verifier and sub-key management code, and run test enrichments.
automation.humanMust: Contact Waterfall or join a sales call, agree to pricing and terms, and approve privacy and compliance use.

uncertain: How the first key is issued, trial credits, rate limits, sandbox, and sub-key use for customers.
The Authentication and API key overview pages were only partly visible.
